source.title: Exact Mean Square Linear Stability Analysis for SGD

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper experimentally examines whether SGD converges at the edge of its mean-square stability region, using stability bounds and sharpness measured at converged minima. It does not test the above-threshold catapult dynamics or the full-batch sharpness trajectory in V5.
record.gate_note: The MNIST experiments vary learning rate and batch size, warm up the learning rate, and report converged-minimum sharpness and stability bounds. Figure-only values are retained as figure-only; cited results from other studies are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures mini-batch SGD's stability bounds and sharpness at converged minima. It does not measure V5's recovery above the initial stability limit, loss and curvature transients, full-batch sharpness hovering while loss falls, or divergence from initially subthreshold rates. The endpoint behavior was deliberately encouraged through large initialization and learning-rate warm-up.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors derive an explicit mean-square linear stability threshold, characterize its batch-size dependence, and validate predictions on MNIST. Their deliberately designed experiments suggest convergence near that boundary in certain regimes; they do not establish V5's training dynamics.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments use single-hidden-layer ReLU networks with quadratic loss on a subset of MNIST, large initialization, and learning-rate warm-up; they assess mean-square stability rather than the training-error outcomes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes the stability threshold and how closely the reported sharpness bounds track 2/η; the text reports B ≥ 32 as behaving similarly to GD for the Figure 1 sharpness comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: For B = 1 and B = 2, the optimized lower bound on generalized sharpness nearly reaches 2/η at converged minima over a wide range of learning rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: With large initialization and learning-rate warm-up, mini-batch SGD can reach minima near its mean-square linear stability boundary.

fits_no_version.finding: Endpoint Hessian sharpness approaches 2/η for moderate batch sizes, with B ≥ 32 behaving similarly to GD in the reported experiment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size affects endpoint sharpness and the proximity of SGD's stability threshold to GD's threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: The study derives an exact local mean-square stability threshold and proves that it is non-decreasing with batch size under its assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linearized SGD near interpolating or regular minima has a batch-dependent mean-square stability threshold.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Conference on Learning Theory (Proceedings of Machine Learning Research, vol. 247, 2024)
record.problems: The experiments use a subset of MNIST and a single-hidden-layer network; the stability analysis is linearized near minima. The optimized bound is found numerically and the authors note that the optimization may fail to find its global optimum for some hyperparameters. Runs not converging within 4 × 10^4 epochs were removed from plots. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported rows beyond the B = 1 and B = 2 edge-of-stability comparisons were retained. Figure 1 reports sharpness versus learning rate and batch size, including B ≥ 32 behavior similar to GD, but these results do not test V5’s stated above-threshold or full-batch trajectory claims.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, random or corrupted labels, and effects of model size, stopping time, and regularization.
Spurious local minima in ReLU teacher-student problems and their reduction through extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation, identity shortcuts, and training deep plain or unnormalized residual networks.
Comparative effects of activation-matched initialization, signal propagation, and orthogonality on training speed and trainable depth.

All specified dynamics: above-initial-threshold recovery, transient loss rise and curvature reduction, divergence at larger rates, full-batch sharpness hovering while loss falls, and divergence despite initially subthreshold rates.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both V5 verdicts. Neither endpoint stability evidence nor untested dynamics justify supports or limits_scope. Figure 1 and the additional batch-size results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR benchmarks, including corrupted or random labels; model size and training duration effects.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual network depth, identity shortcuts, and normalization.
Initialization effects on signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
The experiments do not test learning rates above the initial stability limit, the catapult loss-rise mechanism, full-batch sharpness hovering over time, or the reported divergence cases.
Batch normalization comparisons and Fixup training without normalization.

rows.subject: single hidden-layer ReLU networks
rows.operation_detail: Measured sharpness at converged minima across learning rates with batch size B = 1; compared to stability bounds.

conditions.value: subset of MNIST: 1024 samples from four classes

rows.measure: Sharpness and stability-bound comparison to 2/η; optimized bound (27) is described as coinciding with 2/η over a wide range of step sizes.
rows.note: The text says the optimized bound and 2/η coincide over a wide range for B = 1, supporting convergence at the designed edge of stability; plotted values are not transcribed.
rows.check: The B = 1 endpoint bound coincides with 2/η over a wide range, but this measures generalized mean-square stability at selected converged minima, not any dynamics specified in V5. Only runs reaching loss below 10^-6 for 200 consecutive epochs were retained; runs failing to converge within 40,000 epochs were excluded.

rows.subject: single hidden-layer ReLU networks
rows.operation_detail: Measured sharpness at converged minima across learning rates with batch size B = 2; compared to stability bounds.
rows.measure: Sharpness and stability-bound comparison to 2/η; optimized bound (27) is described as coinciding with 2/η over a wide range of step sizes.
rows.note: The text says the optimized bound and 2/η coincide over a wide range for B = 2, supporting convergence at the designed edge of stability; plotted values are not transcribed.
rows.check: The B = 2 endpoint comparison cannot establish V5's recovery or full-batch trajectory effects. The dataset is the same 1,024-sample, four-class MNIST subset as R1, rather than unrestricted MNIST. Large initialization, warm-up, and exclusion of nonconverged runs apply here too.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: MNIST experiment, mini-batch sizes B = 1 and B = 2, over the plotted learning rates
reader_labels.reason: The authors state that the optimized stability bound coincides with 2/η over a wide range and infer convergence at the edge of stability (R1, R2).
